hierarchy-bundles.visual_critic_note: Ambitious tech demo with clean card UI and smooth morphing transitions, but default Tableau10 palette, dense edge bundles converging chaotically at near-zero tension, and right-side nodes visibly clipping outside the viewport prevent it from feeling deliberately designed.
hierarchy-bundles.encoding_integrity_note: scaleSqrt correctly used for force-layout node radii and partition y-scaling; key functions present on both node and link joins; but the sunburst scaleSqrt y-axis silently distorts ring area relative to data value without annotation, and all other layouts use fixed container-size domains appropriate for topology rather than quantitative magnitude.
hierarchy-bundles.stress_test_note: Easing-params sliders fire `updateLayout()` un-throttled on every `input` event (line 748), launching a fresh 1500ms transition per pixel of drag; no explicit `.interrupt()` guard before new transitions; `countFrames` RAF loops leak across `regenerateAndRender()` calls because the old `animationFrameId` is never canceled on re-init; `d3.drag()` in the force layout has no `.filter()` to prevent mouse/touch double-trigger.
hierarchy-bundles.cognitive_load_note: Single-view-at-a-time layout switching keeps working memory load low, and hover/click fading manages the 300-edge bundle density well, but in the default circle-pack view the bundles converge into a dark tangled mass at low tension that obscures underlying nodes before any interaction — animation quality on 200-node simultaneous morph cannot be assessed from a static screenshot.
